correctness.rationale: The proof enumerates every possible geodesic type (within A, within B, present cross edge, missing cross edge). Its necessary/sufficient predicate is proved directly and each named set contributes once through multinomial category counts. Sharp \(\mu=a+b-2\) and its equality count follow by exhausting the exactly two omitted vertices. An independent BFS graph test compared all coefficients on 40 profiles (49,984 subsets), with 210 additional symbolic finite parameter checks. This finite corroboration is not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is a natural matching-edge perturbation interpolating between classical complete bipartite graphs and crown graphs. Every coefficient of a natural geodesic-visibility counting invariant is determined by a structural orbit-type test, with a polynomial-size exact computation, sharp optimizer count, and coefficientwise monotonicity particular to matching deletion. The known \(t=0\) and \(t=a=b\) formulas do not mechanically imply the intermediate three-parameter result. This offers reusable structural information, not just an arbitrary finite test or a tiny numerical improvement.
